title: Prioritize security findings with Datadog Crown Jewels
summary: Discover your most critical cloud resources automatically with Datadog Crown Jewels, then use business context to prioritize vulnerabilities and misconfigurations.
body_markdown:
Christina DePinto


Senior Product Marketing Manager


Leo Wang


Product Manager


Security teams have more findings than they can realistically remediate. Severity scores, known exploits, and runtime activity can help narrow the list, but they don’t always tell you how important the affected resource is to your business. A critical vulnerability in a rarely used service might receive attention before a high-severity vulnerability in a critical service that’s responsible for authentication. To account for business impact, teams often maintain spreadsheets or tagging conventions that identify their most important assets. But those lists require ongoing maintenance and can quickly fall out of date as environments change.


[Datadog Crown Jewels](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/cloud_security_management/crown_jewels/) , a component of the[Datadog Runtime Prioritization Engine](https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/runtime-prioritization-engine/) , uses Datadog’s existing observability data to automatically identify your most critical cloud resources. By analyzing how services interact and where sensitive data is processed or stored, Crown Jewels builds an inventory of critical resources that you can review and customize. Datadog then applies that context to security findings, helping you prioritize remediation based on the importance of the affected resources.


In this post, we’ll show how you can use Crown Jewels to:


-


Identify your most critical cloud resources automatically


-


Tune detection to match your organization’s definition of critical


-


Prioritize and route findings based on business impact


## Identify your most critical cloud resources automatically


Crown Jewels automatically identifies resources that may be critical to your business based on the telemetry data you already send to Datadog. Instead of manually cataloging assets and assigning criticality tags, you can start with an inventory generated from observed resource behavior and relationships. Crown Jewels uses rule-based detection, so resources are identified through specific evidence in your environment.


Crown Jewels evaluates services, databases, and storage buckets and identifies which ones are potentially critical resources based on signals such as:


-


**Sensitive fields in Application Performance Monitoring (APM) spans:** Services that process sensitive data detected in application traces.


-


**Sensitive fields in logs:** Services associated with sensitive data in logs detected by Datadog’s Sensitive Data Scanner.


-


**Sensitive database columns:** Databases with sensitive column names observed in queries.


-


**Sensitive data at rest:** Storage buckets containing sensitive data detected through Agentless Scanning and Sensitive Data Scanner.


-


**Critical service dependencies:** Services that many other services depend on, identified through the APM Service Map.


Crown Jewels requires no additional Agent configuration or instrumentation, but detection coverage depends on the telemetry data enabled for each resource.


### Review the evidence behind each detection


Each resource that Datadog automatically detects includes a brief reason in the inventory. Selecting it opens a side panel with supporting evidence and links to[APM](https://docs.datadoghq.com/tracing/) ,[Sensitive Data Scanner](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/sensitive_data_scanner/#review-sensitive-data-trends) , or the[APM Service Map](https://docs.datadoghq.com/tracing/services/services_map/) for further investigation. For services that process sensitive data, Crown Jewels identifies the sensitive fields observed in queries and the databases those services accessed.


For example, consider a database that Crown Jewels identifies because it contains sensitive information. The evidence panel can identify the tables and columns associated with the detection, such as` password` ,` email` , and` access_role` . You can use that information to determine whether the database contains information that warrants additional protection and should receive higher priority during vulnerability remediation.


## Tune detection to match your organization’s definition of critical


Crown Jewels lets you customize your inventory to reflect the resources your organization considers most important. Detection rules provide an initial assessment, but a resource that processes sensitive-looking data or has many dependencies may not always be business critical. You can review the evidence behind each detection and decide which resources belong on your list.


For example, a service might be flagged because it processes a URL string that matches a sensitive data detection rule. If the service doesn’t handle information that your organization considers sensitive, you can remove it from the Crown Jewels inventory. Conversely, you might know that an internal service supports a critical business function even though Datadog hasn’t detected any of the configured detection rules. You can manually add that service to the inventory, or create tag-based rules for greater customization.


Crown Jewels also lets you enable or disable individual automatic detection rules at the organization level. If dependency-based detection identifies too many low-priority services in your environment, you can disable that rule while keeping sensitive data detection enabled. Teams that already have an established process for identifying critical resources can disable automatic detection and maintain the inventory manually.


Crown Jewels removes resources it automatically detected when they no longer match enabled rules, which helps keep the inventory current as your environment changes.


## Prioritize and route findings based on business impact


Crown Jewels adds business-critical resource context to security findings so you can focus remediation on vulnerabilities and misconfigurations that affect your most important assets. Findings associated with a crown jewel receive the following tag:` @risk.is_crown_jewel:true` .


You can use this tag in[Datadog Cloud Security](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/cloud_security_management) to filter findings by resource criticality and combine it with other criteria, such as severity. For example, consider an environment where the crown jewel filter narrows approximately 620 critical findings to 170, which is a reduction of roughly 73%. The following screenshot shows the resulting view, which gives the team a smaller queue to investigate first:


You can also save filtered views as recurring triage queues and build dashboards to track findings associated with crown jewels over time. For example, a security team can maintain a view of critical vulnerabilities on crown jewel resources and use it during regular remediation reviews. As the underlying inventory changes, the crown jewel context helps the team continue focusing on findings associated with resources that Datadog identifies as critical.


### Extend prioritization to related infrastructure


Crown Jewels also marks findings on infrastructure related to critical services. For example, if a virtual machine supports a crown jewel service, a misconfiguration affecting that machine can be marked as a crown jewel finding. Similarly, a vulnerability in a container image used by a crown jewel service can receive the same criticality context. You can review the related hosts and container images in the Compute Stack section of the Crown Jewels side panel to understand which infrastructure is associated with a critical resource.


Crown Jewels supports several workflows for using this context across Cloud Security, including:


-


[Vulnerability Explorer](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/cloud_security_management/vulnerabilities) : Filter vulnerabilities to prioritize remediation work on critical resources and their dependencies.


-


[Misconfiguration Explorer](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/cloud_security_management/misconfigurations/) : Identify configuration issues affecting business-critical resources so you can focus hardening efforts.


-


[Notifications](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/notifications/) : Configure notification rules that route findings associated with crown jewels differently from other security findings.


-


[Findings Automation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/automation_pipelines/) : Define custom remediation patterns for findings associated with critical resources.


## Focus remediation on your most critical cloud resources


Datadog Crown Jewels helps security teams identify business-critical cloud resources from existing telemetry data and use that context to prioritize security findings. By combining automatic detection with reviewable evidence and customizable rules, Crown Jewels reduces the manual work of maintaining a critical asset inventory and helps teams focus remediation on the resources with the greatest potential business impact.


To learn more about identifying and managing critical resources, read the[Crown Jewels documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/cloud_security_management/crown_jewels/) . You can also explore how the[Runtime Prioritization Engine](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/cloud_security_management/triage_and_prioritize/runtime_prioritization_engine/) combines business criticality with other risk factors to help prioritize security findings.


To get started,[open Crown Jewels in Datadog](https://app.datadoghq.com/security/configuration/crown-jewels) to review your critical resources and use the` @risk.is_crown_jewel:true` filter to prioritize findings associated with them.
